senses.gloss:
piśāca
(‘eater of flesh,’ ‘a goblin’)
------------------------------------------
Belief in devils, goblins, elves and evil spirits is common to almost all the people of the world.
In the Hindu epics and mythological works they are called variously as bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, yakṣas and so on.
Out of these, the piśācas, the ड़्लेस्ह्-एअतिन्ग् and blood-drinking evil spirits, are the most malevolent, bent upon harming others. However, being created by ब्रह्मा, they too have a place in his च्रेअतिओन्!
They are unclean spirits confined to the अन्तरिक्ष (the middle regions). They also live in unclean and barren places.
In some पुराणस् they are described as belonging to the court of कुबेर, the king of Yakṣas ruling at Alakāpurī. In some other पुराणस् they are depicted as devotees of शिव and living on the Muñjavān mountain.
